metadata.desc: An intelligent long-term memory plugin with hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector + graph), WebUI management, and dynamic lifecycle. Supports session/persona isolation, importance decay, and auto-cleanup.

bot_language.hint: Set the language for plugin commands and status replies. zh=Chinese (default), en=English, ru=Russian, ja=Japanese.

access_control.hint: Limit who can use long-term memory and map identities to consistent names across platforms.

whitelist_enabled.hint: When enabled, only listed users, groups, or sessions can capture, summarize, recall, or use Agent memory tools. An empty list denies all memory operations.

allowed_ids.hint: Enter one user ID, platform:user ID, group ID, or full session ID per line. Commas and semicolons are also supported.

identity_aliases.hint: Enter one source=canonical name mapping per line. The source may be platform:user ID, user ID, or current username, for example telegram:12345=Alex.

provider_settings.hint: Configure the AI models used by the memory system

embedding_provider_id.hint: Required: ID of an enabled Embedding Provider in AstrBot (for example openai_embedding). Leaving it empty only falls back to the first available Embedding Provider and may pick the wrong model or break vector/graph index initialization. Create and enable an Embedding Provider in the AstrBot LLM settings first, then fill in its ID here.

llm_provider_id.hint: The large language model ID used for summarizing conversations and evaluating memory importance. Leave blank to use AstrBot default. A model with strong reasoning capabilities is recommended.

llm_fallback_provider_ids.hint: Provider IDs to try in order when the primary LLM fails (JSON array, e.g. ["openai_gpt-4o","gemini-2.5-pro"]). Switches on timeout, rate limit (429), 5xx or authentication failures; parsing/format errors do not switch. Leave empty to disable fallback.

llm_call_timeout_seconds.hint: Timeout for a single call to each provider. On timeout the provider is treated as unavailable and the next one is tried. Allowed range: 5-600.

llm_stream_mode.hint: How memory processing calls the LLM. auto (default): try non-streaming first and switch to streaming automatically when the provider reports that non-stream requests are unsupported; always: always stream (for providers that only accept stream=true); never: always non-streaming (previous behavior).

session_manager.hint: Manage user session states and conversation history caching behavior

enable_full_group_capture.hint: Whether to capture all messages in group chats, including messages that do not mention the bot. When enabled, every group message is recorded to build richer group-chat context.

max_sessions.hint: Maximum number of sessions kept in memory (LRU eviction). Once exceeded, the least recently used session is removed from cache, but data remains in the database. Allowed range: 1-10000.

session_ttl.hint: Sessions inactive for longer than this duration are removed from cache. Default is 3600 (1 hour). Allowed range: 60-86400.

context_window_size.hint: Maximum number of historical messages passed to the LLM. Larger values provide richer context but consume more tokens. Recommended: 20-100. Allowed range: 1-1000.

max_messages_per_session.hint: Maximum number of historical messages retained per session in the database. When exceeded, only the oldest summarized messages are deleted to avoid losing unsummarized context. Allowed range: 100-10000.

cleanup_batch_size.hint: Minimum number of old summarized messages to delete per batch when the session history exceeds the limit. A value too small will cause only a few messages to be deleted each round after overflow. Allowed range: 1-1000.

recall_engine.hint: Control memory retrieval and injection into conversations

top_k.hint: Number of most relevant memories returned per retrieval. Set to 0 to skip automatic recall/injection while keeping historical injection cleanup. Recommended: 3-10. Allowed range: 0-50.

max_k.hint: Maximum memories returned when the Agent actively calls the long-term memory retrieval tool. Used to limit single-tool recall scale. Recommended: 5-10. Allowed range: 1-50.

importance_weight.hint: Weight coefficient for memory importance in the hybrid scoring. Higher values prioritize high-importance memories. Allowed range: 0-10.

min_importance_for_retrieval.hint: Filter out memories below this importance value. Range: 0-1. Set to 0 to disable filtering.

min_similarity_for_retrieval.hint: Filter vector candidates below this similarity. Keyword-only matches remain eligible. Default 0.45; set to 0 to disable the filter.

recent_memory_count.hint: Only fill remaining slots with recent memories in the current scope when relevant results are fewer than the requested count. Fixed slots are no longer reserved. Default 0 (disabled).

recent_memory_max_age_hours.hint: Only memories inside this age window qualify for reserved recent slots. Set to 0 for no age limit. Allowed range: 0-8760.

memory_type_filter.hint: Recall all memories, or exclude memories known to contain only preferences or relationships. Legacy untyped memories remain eligible.

fallback_to_vector.hint: Automatically fall back to pure vector search when hybrid retrieval fails or returns empty results. Recommended to keep enabled.

rerank_enabled.hint: After RRF fusion, call a Rerank model to reorder candidate memories by query relevance, replacing the RRF ranking as the relevance score source. Requires a Rerank-type provider configured in AstrBot.

rerank_provider_id.hint: The ID of a Rerank-type provider in AstrBot. Leave empty to skip reranking even when enabled.

rerank_candidates.hint: Number of fused candidate memories sent to the Rerank model; only top_k are kept after reranking. Larger values improve ranking accuracy but increase per-recall Rerank API cost. Recommended 10-30. (Range: 2-100)

fusion_mode.hint: How BM25 and vector results are fused: score weights normalized scores (default); rrf uses reciprocal rank fusion.

fusion_bm25_weight.hint: Weight of the BM25 route in score fusion; the vector route uses one minus this value. Range 0-1.

fusion_agreement_bonus.hint: Score bonus added when the same memory is hit by both the BM25 and vector routes. Range 0-1.

recall_candidate_multiplier.hint: Each route returns top_k times this many candidates before fusion. Larger values widen recall but cost more time. Range 1-10.

injection_method.hint: Memories are appended to the current user message as a mark_as_temp temporary part that AstrBot filters out when saving history, so injection never touches conversation history or the prefix cache.

auto_remove_injected.hint: Automatically remove injection fragments left in conversation history by legacy injection modes from the request context before injecting new ones (the current add-only injection never leaves residue). Recommended to keep enabled.

inject_with_recent_context.hint: When enabled, memory retrieval appends the recent two dialogue turns to the current query, improving relevance for follow-up questions and reducing unrelated recalls.

recent_context_max_age_seconds.hint: Only historical messages within this time range extend the recall query. Set to 0 to disable the time limit. Allowed range: 0-604800.

search_cache_enabled.hint: Reuse retrieval results for the same session and query within a short time window to reduce repeated SQLite and FAISS work during follow-up conversations.

search_cache_ttl_seconds.hint: How long retrieval cache entries are kept. Writes, updates, and deletes invalidate the cache automatically. Set to 0 to disable caching. Allowed range: 0-600.

search_cache_max_size.hint: Maximum number of retrieval results kept in memory. When the limit is exceeded, the least recently used entries are evicted. Allowed range: 0-10000.

private_memory_notice_enabled.hint: Append a notice to injected memories marked visibility=private and disclosed=false, stating that the assistant experienced this privately and the user has not been told. Disable to omit the notice.

tokenizer.hint: jieba: word-level segmentation with better recall; reserves ~55 MB after first use. builtin: built-in single-character/ASCII tokens, never imports jieba and saves memory. Run /lmem rebuild-index after switching.

importance_decay.hint: Gradually reduce the importance of old memories over time to prevent outdated information from retaining high weight indefinitely

decay_rate.hint: Proportion of memory importance decayed per day. Default 0.005 means a 0.5% decrease daily; access reduces the effective decay rate. Set to 0 to disable decay. Allowed range: 0-1.

access_decay_window_days.hint: Memories accessed within this window reduce their effective decay rate according to access count. Allowed range: 1-3650.

access_decay_max_count.hint: The access count that grants maximum decay protection. Additional accesses beyond this count do not increase protection further. Allowed range: 1-10000.

access_count_decay_multiplier.hint: After each daily decay pass, access counts are multiplied by this ratio so old hot memories do not stay protected forever. Allowed range: 0-1.

protected_importance_threshold.hint: Memories at or above this importance do not participate in daily importance decay. Default 0.6 protects memories at 60%+ importance. Allowed range: 0-1.

fusion_strategy.hint: Fusion parameters for BM25 and vector search results (internally uses the RRF algorithm)

rrf_k.hint: Lower values emphasize top-ranked results; higher values produce smoother fusion. Recommended: 30-120. Default is 60. Allowed range: 1-1000.

use_persona_filtering.hint: When enabled, only memories related to the current persona are recalled. Memories of different personas do not interfere with each other.

use_session_filtering.hint: Used only when Memory Scope Mode is Legacy. When enabled, each session is isolated; when disabled, memories are not filtered by session.

memory_scope_mode.hint: Legacy preserves existing settings; Per Session isolates each origin; Per User shares memory across chats for the same platform user; Global shares memory everywhere. Switching the mode does not migrate existing memories: run /lmem migrate-scope <target> apply.

isolated_sessions.hint: Enter one full session ID per line. These sessions always use their own memory scope, overriding Per User, Global, and disabled legacy session filtering.

reflection_engine.hint: Control when conversation summarization is triggered and memories are generated

summary_trigger_rounds.hint: Trigger a summary and write it to memory after this many rounds of dialogue (one question and one answer counts as one round). Allowed range: 1-100.

window_split_by_day.hint: When enabled, conversations spanning multiple days are not merged into one memory: a summary covers only the oldest day, and newer parts wait for later triggers.

window_split_gap_minutes.hint: When the gap between adjacent messages exceeds this many minutes, only the oldest segment is summarized; 0 = do not split by idle gap. Allowed range: 0-1440.

include_source_time_tags.hint: Derive source dates from original message timestamps and store them without relying on LLM inference.

source_retention_importance_threshold.hint: Store original messages separately when summary importance reaches this value, enabling verification, detailed Agent recall, and re-summarization. Range 0-1; 1 keeps only maximum-importance memories.

max_segments_per_run.hint: Maximum number of day/idle-split segments summarized in one trigger. Remaining backlog is consumed on the next trigger. (Allowed range: 1–50)

agent_tools.hint: Control whether AstrBot Agent receives tools for active long-term memory recall and writing.

enable_recall_tool.hint: When enabled, registers recall_long_term_memory so the Agent can actively search long-term memories.

enable_agentic_recall_beta.hint: Experimental; requires the active recall tool enabled above. When on, recall_long_term_memory is enhanced (current-speaker lookup, time-range filters, exclude seen candidates), the read_memory_evidence deep-read tool is added, and an agentic recall policy is injected. Search and deep read share a per-request budget. Turning it off restores the legacy recall behavior. Takes effect for new requests after saving and a successful reload.

enable_memorize_tool.hint: When enabled, registers memorize_long_term_memory so the Agent can actively write long-term memories.

enable_forget_tool.hint: When enabled, registers forget_long_term_memory. Admin-only; it only archives (soft-deletes) memories, never physically deletes them, and an admin can restore them from the WebUI memory page (set status back to active). Off by default.

forget_tool_max_memories.description: Forget tool max memories per call
forget_tool_max_memories.hint: Maximum number of memories a single tool call may archive; a larger request is rejected entirely. (Allowed: 1-10)

forget_tool_cooldown_seconds.hint: Minimum interval between two successful archives in the same session; calls during the cooldown are rejected. 0 = disabled. (Allowed: 0-3600)

agentic_recall_max_calls.hint: Shared per-request call budget for the memory search and deep-read tools. Suggested 3-6. (Allowed: 1-20)

agentic_recall_time_budget_seconds.hint: Total working time for memory tools since the first call of this request; when exceeded, recall stops and the model answers with evidence already gathered. Suggested 10-60. (Allowed: 1-300)

agentic_recall_max_result_chars.description: Max chars per agentic tool result
agentic_recall_max_result_chars.hint: Maximum characters a Beta memory tool returns in one call; longer content can be read via pagination. Suggested 4000-30000. (Allowed: 500-100000)

enable_profile_tool.hint: Register update_user_profile so the agent can write the user profile proactively; writes use the same evidence/confidence rules and record history. Off by default.

graph_memory.hint: When enabled, both document-based and graph-based paths are maintained simultaneously, each supporting keyword and vector retrieval, with results unified into a single fused recall set.

enabled.hint: When enabled, graph nodes, edges, and graph vector indexes are automatically built. Recommended to keep enabled.

document_route_weight.hint: The proportion of the document path fusion score in the final dual-path ranking. Allowed range: 0-1.

graph_route_weight.hint: The proportion of the graph path fusion score in the final dual-path ranking. Allowed range: 0-1.

cross_route_bonus.hint: Extra score added when the same memory is hit by both the document path and the graph path. Allowed range: 0-0.5.

expansion_limit.hint: Maximum number of candidate entries expanded from hit nodes to their neighbors during graph keyword retrieval. Allowed range: 1-200.

expansion_hops.hint: Number of hops expanded outward from matched nodes during graph keyword retrieval. Default is 1; setting it to 2 can recall indirect relations with a small query-cost increase. Allowed range: 1-2.

second_hop_weight.hint: Score weight for second-hop graph candidates. Higher values make indirect relations more likely to enter the final recall results. Allowed range: 0-1.

dynamic_route_weighting.hint: Automatically adjust document-route and graph-route weights according to relationship, time, and definition-like intent in the query.

max_topics_per_memory.hint: Maximum number of topic nodes extracted from a single memory. Allowed range: 1-20.

max_participants_per_memory.hint: Maximum number of participant nodes extracted from a single memory. Allowed range: 1-30.

max_facts_per_memory.hint: Maximum number of key facts extracted from a single memory to enter the graph index. Allowed range: 1-30.

atom_enabled.hint: When enabled, each key_fact becomes an independent memory atom with its own lifetime and decay curve. When disabled, the plugin falls back to the original coarse-grained behavior.

atom_maintenance_interval_hours.hint: How often the lifecycle manager runs expiration and forgetting checks for memory atoms. Allowed range: 1-168.

atom_forget_delay_days.hint: How many days after expiration an atom is completely removed from retrieval indexes. Allowed range: 1-90.

atom_purge_delay_days.hint: How many days after removal from retrieval indexes a forgotten atom is physically deleted from the database to reclaim storage. Allowed range: 1-365.

channel_memory.hint: When enabled, group summaries are stored in a shared channel scope so any member of the group can recall them; recall searches the current scope and the channel scope together within one top_k budget. Disabled keeps the previous behavior.

enabled.hint: Group summaries are stored under livingmemory:channel:<platform>:<group id>; personal memories (private summaries and explicit writes) keep their own scopes.

min_user_slots.hint: Personal/session results kept at minimum during merged recall; channel results fill any gap. (Allowed: 0-5)

min_channel_slots.hint: Channel results kept at minimum during merged recall; personal results fill any gap. (Allowed: 0-5)

include_archived.description: Include archived memories in channel recall
include_archived.hint: Off by default: archived memories stay excluded. When on, only channel-scope results relax the status filter.

migration_settings.hint: Control database version upgrade behavior on plugin startup

auto_migrate.hint: Automatically detect and upgrade outdated database versions on plugin startup. Recommended to keep enabled.

create_backup.hint: Automatically create a backup file before performing database migration to prevent data loss in case of migration failure. Recommended to keep enabled.

index_rebuild_settings.hint: Control batch size, Embedding request rate, and failure tolerance for the /lmem rebuild-index command. Low-spec cloud servers should keep concurrency small.

batch_size.hint: Number of memories read from the documents table per batch. Larger values increase memory peak and affect more entries on failure. Recommended: 25-100. Allowed range: 1-500.

embedding_batch_size.hint: Number of texts included in a single Embedding API request. Reduce further if the provider has strict TPM rate limits. Allowed range: 1-256.

tasks_limit.hint: Internal concurrency limit for batch Embedding. To avoid triggering API rate limits, the default is 1. Allowed range: 1-8.

max_retries.hint: Maximum retry attempts for a failed Embedding batch. Allowed range: 1-8.

retry_base_delay.hint: Base wait time for exponential backoff after a batch failure. At least 30 seconds will be waited when encountering 429/TPM rate limits. Allowed range: 0-60.

batch_delay.hint: Additional wait time between each documents read batch, used to proactively reduce overall rebuild rate. Allowed range: 0-10.

request_delay.hint: Wait time between each Embedding API sub-request. Increase this first if 429/TPM is triggered frequently. Allowed range: 0-60.

max_failure_ratio.hint: During full vector rebuild, the new index will only be switched if the failure ratio does not exceed this value. 0.02 means up to 2% failure is allowed. Allowed range: 0-1.

backup_settings.hint: Create daily memory backups and prune daily backups past retention plus stale version backups so the data directory cannot grow without bound

enabled.hint: Automatically back up the database after daily decay tasks. Recommended to keep enabled.

keep_days.hint: Retention days for daily and version backups. Version backups additionally keep only the 2 most recent ones, and total backup size is pruned from the oldest when it exceeds 512 MB. Default 7 days. Allowed range: 1-365.

forgetting_agent.hint: Archive (by default, instead of deleting) aged low-importance memories to keep the memory store and indexes bounded

auto_cleanup_enabled.hint: Automatically clean up eligible old memories after daily importance decay.

auto_archived_enabled.hint: Enabled by default: cleanup candidates are removed from retrieval indexes and kept as restorable archived documents. Disable to delete them instead.

cleanup_days_threshold.hint: Memories older than this many days become cleanup candidates. Default 120 days; they are processed only if importance is also below the threshold. Allowed range: 1-3650.

cleanup_importance_threshold.hint: Only memories with importance below this value are cleaned up. Default 0.25 means memories below 25% importance. Allowed range: 0-1.

memory_consolidation.hint: Periodically aggregate, organize, and summarize scattered low-value memories into more concise ones to control memory store size at the source

enabled.hint: When enabled, eligible scattered memories are automatically merged into concise summaries. Recommended when the memory store grows large.

trigger.hint: daily = run on the daily schedule; reflection = also check and run alongside each reflection.

granularity.hint: session = aggregate within the same session; semantic = cluster across sessions by semantic similarity.

keep_original.hint: archive = keep originals as archived (removed from retrieval but restorable); delete = remove originals permanently.

min_memories_per_group.hint: A group must contain at least this many memories to trigger consolidation, avoiding unnecessary LLM calls. Allowed range: 2-50.

min_age_days.hint: Only consolidate memories older than this many days, avoiding recently-updated memories. Allowed range: 0-3650.

max_importance.hint: Only consolidate memories with importance below this value; high-importance memories stay untouched. Allowed range: 0-1.

max_groups_per_run.hint: Limits how many groups are consolidated per run to avoid triggering too many LLM calls at once. Allowed range: 1-100.

semantic_similarity_threshold.hint: In semantic mode, two memories are grouped only when their similarity reaches this value. Allowed range: 0-1.

enabled.hint: Before storing a summary memory, compare it with recent memories in the same session/persona; at or above the threshold, merge into the existing memory instead of adding a new one.

similarity_threshold.hint: Vector similarity threshold for merging; higher is more conservative. 0.90–0.95 is recommended.

max_candidates.hint: Number of recent memories compared on each check.

merge_sources.hint: Append new source messages to the existing memory when merging, for review and re-summarization.

max_source_messages.hint: Maximum number of source messages kept on a merged memory.

profile_settings.hint: Maintain a structured, versioned user profile per memory scope + persona. Updated incrementally during summaries and injected as a fixed short block on recall. Enabled by default; no extra LLM calls.

enabled.hint: Merge summary output into the user profile and inject the profile block on every recall; disable to stop all profile reads/writes.

max_chars.hint: Maximum characters for the injected profile text, independent of the memory injection budget. Larger values keep more detail but consume more context. (50–2000)

min_confidence.hint: Profile updates only apply directly when confidence reaches this value and evidence is valid; otherwise they become pending candidates. (0–1)

history_limit.hint: Number of history versions kept per profile; oldest versions are trimmed without deleting the current profile. (1–200)

max_pending.hint: Low-confidence or evidence-less updates go to the pending list; oldest candidates are dropped beyond this limit. (1–500)

trace_settings.hint: Record explainable traces of every memory recall (candidates, routes, rejection reasons, final injection) to debug why a memory was or was not recalled. In-memory ring buffer only; disk persistence is opt-in and query text is not stored by default.

enabled.hint: When disabled the recall path records nothing and behaves exactly as before.

max_records.hint: Number of recent traces kept in the in-process ring buffer; 0 disables the buffer. Oldest records are overwritten.

persist_enabled.hint: Append one JSON object per line to recall_traces/YYYYMMDD.jsonl in the data directory. Disabled by default to avoid continuous disk writes.

include_query_text.hint: By default only a query hash is stored; enabling this includes the user's raw query in traces, so enable it with privacy in mind.

max_file_mb.hint: New traces stop being appended to a JSONL file once it reaches this size.

retention_days.hint: JSONL trace files older than this are cleaned up on the next write.

external_api.hint: Let external agent terminals read and write memories with API keys (disabled by default). Create keys with /lmem apikey or the dashboard, then use the bundled MCP bridge.

enabled.hint: Starts a dedicated HTTP listener (default 127.0.0.1:7801) serving /page/external. When disabled every external endpoint returns 404. Reload the plugin after changing.

listen_host.hint: Bind address for the external API. Keep loopback 127.0.0.1 and let a reverse proxy expose it, if needed.

listen_port.hint: Port for the external API listener, default 7801. Reload the plugin after changing.

max_request_bytes.hint: Largest accepted request body, default 262144 (256 KiB); larger requests return 400.

default_rate_limit_per_min.hint: Default per-key request budget for new keys; can be overridden per key.

default_write_limit_per_min.hint: Default per-key write budget for new keys. Read requests do not consume it.

audit_retention_days.hint: Audit JSONL lives in the plugin data directory (external_api_audit.jsonl) and is trimmed to this many days, default 30.

trust_proxy_headers.hint: Use X-Forwarded-For as the audit client address. Enable only behind a trusted reverse proxy.

dashboard.title: Memory Dashboard
dashboard.description: Browse, edit, and curate long-term memories.
